$comment: EXAMPLE ONLY. Every price below is a placeholder, not a quote.
Provider rate cards change; copy this file, then replace each figure with the
current published rate for the model you are actually calling. Roundhouse
reports savings against these numbers, so a stale rate card does not produce a
slightly wrong dashboard -- it produces a confidently wrong one.
Point ROUNDHOUSE_CATALOG at your copy.
"providers" says where each model's `provider` actually is: a base URL, the
path each dialect is served at, the environment variable its key arrives in,
and any static headers the gateway asks for. A model whose `provider` names
no entry here is refused at load -- with one exception, "openai", which this
build defines implicitly at the endpoint ROUNDHOUSE_OPENAI_API_BASE names, so
a catalog written before providers existed still loads unchanged. The key
itself is never in this file: `auth.env` names the variable, and the
credential a turn actually authenticates with is resolved per turn from the
control plane's three tiers (deployment, project, member).
"openrouter" and "anthropic" below are real, dispatchable definitions: point
OPENROUTER_API_KEY or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY at a real key and this build has a client
for both dialects. "dynamo-fleet" is not -- it is a template for the shape a
self-hosted Dynamo deployment or switchyard-server (base_url is your own
frontend, serving chat_completions) would use, and nothing in "models" names it,
so it validates without a client. That absence is deliberate and this file is
the reason: a "models" entry speaking a dialect this build cannot serialize
stops the boot -- by design, since the alternative is failing one tenant's turn
for a line in a file -- and it stops it the moment ROUNDHOUSE_FRONTIER_UPSTREAM
names a real upstream, which is exactly what the README tells an operator to do
next. An example that cannot boot the binary it ships with teaches the format
wrong. Copy the definition, replace the placeholders, and add entries that name
it once your build carries a client for that dialect.
The "anthropic" entry is a template like "openai": the definition above it is
real, the model name is yours to fill in, and its prices are zeros for the same
reason every other price here is. Note its cache_model is "deterministic" rather
than "inactivity_decay" -- Anthropic caches only what an explicit cache_control
breakpoint names, and for a fixed TTL, which is a different prediction from
OpenAI's automatic decay and is why the two dialects carry different models.
Its cache_write_per_mtok_usd is the one price on this dialect you must not leave
at zero once you fill the card in: zero means "this provider does not price the
write separately", not "writes are free", and Anthropic does price it.
One provider serves one dialect. The registry holds one transport per provider
name, so a provider whose "models" entries speak two wire_protocols stops the
boot -- OpenRouter serves both /responses and /messages, so if you want both,
define it twice under two names pointing at the same base_url.
"openrouter-messages" is that second definition, written out so the pattern is
not just described. It is also where auth.style lives, which matters on this
dialect and no other: a stored key is spelled "x_api_key" unless the definition
says otherwise -- Anthropic's own convention, and api.anthropic.com answers a
bearer with a 401 whose message does not say why -- while OpenRouter's /messages
route authenticates only on Authorization: Bearer and answers an x-api-key with
"Missing Authentication header". So set "style": "bearer" there and leave the
field off everywhere else. A spelling this build does not send is refused at
load, naming the provider and the field; getting it wrong the other way is a
401 on every turn, which reads like a bad key rather than a wrong file. Nothing
under "models" names openrouter-messages yet -- point a Claude model on
OpenRouter at it and it dispatches.
The three entries under "openrouter" spell out full, dated model ids rather
than a placeholder, because that is the point they demonstrate: an id with no
date suffix is not a rolling pointer to "whatever is newest" the way
"~deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-latest" is -- deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-0731 is
itself a frozen snapshot dated 2026-07-31, and the *bare* deepseek ids (no
-NNNN suffix at all, e.g. deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash) are frozen too, pinned to
an earlier snapshot rather than tracking forward. Write the full dated id you
mean; "the latest DeepSeek" is ambiguous and this catalog has no mechanism to
re-resolve it later -- which is why a "~"-prefixed id under "openrouter" is now
refused at load rather than only discouraged here: the rule was worth stating,
so it was worth enforcing where the ambiguity is still cheap to remove.
openai/gpt-5.6-sol shows the same model reachable through
two different `provider` entries -- directly as "openai", or, as written
here, through "openrouter" -- which the catalog treats as two independent
prices and two independent (provider, model) identities, never one deduplicated
against the other.

correlaries.note: Replace this note with why. It is shown verbatim on the dashboard, because a reader deciding whether to trust the savings figure is really deciding whether to trust this sentence.
